per_case.playbook: Isolate 192.168.100.147 from the network. Preserve forensic images, review running processes and scheduled tasks, hunt for lateral-movement tooling and credential dumps, rotate all credentials associated with the host, and correlate with the destination host 192.168.100.3 to determine whether the HTTP service was successfully abused.

Isolate host 192.168.100.148 from the network immediately to prevent further brute force/service abuse attacks against 192.168.100.3. Investigate the host for malware, bot infection, or credential compromise that enabled the automated attack behavior. Identify the initial access vector, contain the threat, and preserve forensic evidence for incident response.

ISOLATE_HOST - Immediately isolate 192.168.100.149 from the network. Preserve forensic images, kill the Metasploit listener on port 4444, and investigate the C2 peer 192.168.100.6 for the same compromise. Block internal traffic to 192.168.100.6:4444 at the switch/firewall level. Perform full malware analysis and review for lateral movement to other hosts.

Isolate 192.168.100.150 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images, then investigate for initial access vector and malware. Block outbound connections to 192.168.100.3 on ports 80 and 50032. Rotate credentials for any accounts that operated from this host and review 192.168.100.3 for signs of successful compromise.

Isolate 192.168.100.3 from the network immediately. Block egress to 13.54.166.67 (external C2) at the firewall. Perform forensic imaging, inspect for IoT/MQTT malware or botnet agent processes, review for lateral movement to the 7 internal hosts that contacted it, and rotate any credentials/keys on affected segments. Hunt peer hosts (192.168.100.5, .6, .7, .55, .150) for similar beaconing behavior.

Immediately isolate 192.168.100.6 from the network (disconnect/vLAN quarantine). Preserve a forensic disk and memory image before remediation. Block and investigate the C2 peer 192.168.100.149 (port 4444) — treat it as a C2 server and exfil destination. Investigate lateral movement to 192.168.100.3:80 and the 4 beaconing hosts (192.168.100.147, .148, .149, .150) for shared IOCs. Hunt for the initial access vector, rotate credentials on affected systems, and rebuild 192.168.100.6 from known-good media.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 162.208.22.34 at the perimeter firewall/egress filtering. Concurrently investigate and isolate the 6 internal source hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15) as they are the compromised trojan agents beaconing outbound. Block outbound connections to this IP across all internal hosts and initiate malware remediation on the affected endpoints.

Isolate 192.168.10.255 from the network immediately to prevent further lateral beaconing. Perform forensic imaging, identify the Trojan/C2 binary and persistence mechanism, and review the 13 internal source hosts that beacon to it for co-mromise. Block NetBIOS (137/138) egress at the firewall and hunt for similar internal C2 patterns across the environment.

IGNORE - No action required. These are benign service-pattern false positives. Document the analysis and close the alerts. Optionally tune the flow sensor to distinguish DNS query/response traffic (port 53, single-packet UDP, short duration) from genuine floods, and avoid flagging multi-service internal servers as C2 receivers.

Close as false positive. No host isolation or IP blocking required. The DNS traffic to 192.168.10.3:53 is normal resolution activity. If alerting volume on DNS flow counts remains high, tune the FLOW-002 rule to exclude internal DNS servers (port 53 to known internal resolvers) to reduce false positives. No further action needed on 192.168.10.5.

Isolate host 192.168.10.8 from the network immediately. Block outbound traffic to 205.174.165.73 and port 444 at the firewall. Perform forensic imaging, then investigate for the initial access vector and malware (check for Metasploit/Reverse_TCP implants on port 444). Preserve the network_traffic records as evidence. Do NOT block the IP or treat this as benign — the internal host is the compromised actor.

No action required. Dismiss both FLOW-002 and FLOW-005 alerts as false positives. Optionally tune the flow sensor to reduce DNS-query-volume and multi-host-connection false positives. Continue routine monitoring; no isolation or blocking needed.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 23.60.139.27 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter (block all traffic to/from 23.60.139.27, port 80). Since 11 internal hosts are beaconing to this C2, initiate a separate host-compromise investigation (ISOLATE_HOST) on the internal source hosts to identify and remediate the malware. Add the C2 IP to the blocklist and monitor for reconnection attempts via alternate ports or DNS-based C2.

Block 50.63.243.230 at the perimeter firewall/egress proxy immediately and add it to the threat blocklist. Since the 11 internal hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .51) are the compromised beacons, initiate ISOLATE_HOST remediation on those endpoints — hunt for the malware/C2 implant, capture the beaconing payload, and preserve forensic images. Correlate DNS/HTTP request data in session_data to identify the actual C2 domain or command channel.
